newsitem.title: GERMANY: EMU delay possible if big states miss targets - Buba.
newsitem.headline: EMU delay possible if big states miss targets - Buba.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said on Monday that a delay of European currency union could be considered if it was clear big countries will fail to meet the Maastricht treaty convergence criteria.
"If it is the case that the big countries fail to meet the criteria, than a delay could be considered," Tietmeyer said in a panel discussion before a banking audience here.
Tietmeyer added that, if it was clear that countries would not be able to meet the single currency criteria in time for the January 1, 1999 launch, "it would be better to say so sooner."
In an earlier speech, however, he said the Bundesbank was operating on the assumption the single currency would be launched on time.
He said the currency union should be based on strict, narrow and sustainable adherance to the Maastricht economic convergence criteria.
Tietmeyer also said it was premature to speculate on which countries would make it into the single currency club.
Both Germany and France last week denied reports they were hatching a plot to exclude heavily-indebted Italy and with it Spain from joining the starting EMU lineup.
European leaders will decide in a year which countries are elible to join EMU on the basis of an appraisal by European central bankers of their adherance to the Maastrict criteria.
Germany has pledged to achieve the Maastricht deficit target of three percent of gross domestic product.
